To: posts/new
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: Correction: GST formula error in the takings template (v1.0 to v1.2)

If you downloaded my daily takings and GST template before 8 November, please read this before you file your next return.

**What was wrong**

Column F worked out GST by multiplying your takings by 9%. That is only correct if the amounts you key in exclude GST. Most hawkers and many cafes display GST-inclusive prices, so the takings you key in already have the GST inside them. For those amounts, the GST portion is 9/109 of the total, not 9%.

Ravi's figures show the difference. His takings on 3 November were $1,090, GST inclusive. The template showed GST of $98.10. The correct GST is $90. The sheet overstated it by $8.10, which works out to about 9% more GST than was actually due. The same thing happened on every day's row, and the overstated figures carried into the quarterly summary.

The Box 1 sales total on the quarterly tab is calculated separately and was correct. Only Box 6, the output tax figure, was affected.

**How I missed it**

Before releasing v1.0, I tested the template against my own sample figures. Those figures were already GST-exclusive, so 9% gave the right answer and the check passed. I did not test it the way most of you actually use it. That was my mistake. The error was carried into v1.1 (2 Sep) and v1.2 (1 Oct) because neither update touched column F. The template has been downloaded 412 times since 12 August.

**Who is affected**

You are affected if you used v1.0, v1.1 or v1.2 and keyed in GST-inclusive takings. If you keyed in amounts that genuinely excluded GST, your column F figures were correct.

Because the error overstates GST, nobody will have underpaid IRAS. Some of you may have overpaid. That is not a comfort if it is your money, and Melvin is right to be upset. People used this sheet because an accountant put it up, and that trust should have come with proper checking. I am sorry it did not.

**The fix**

v1.3, uploaded 8 November, is on the original post. It has a new setting in cell H2. Set it to match the amounts you key in:

- Choose "prices exclude GST" only if your entries exclude GST.
- Use the inclusive setting if your entries are the receipts you actually collected, including GST. This applies even if your menu prices are shown before GST. What matters is the amount you key in, not how the menu is printed.

**If you already filed Q3 using the old sheet**

1. Download v1.3. Keep your old file as it is and do not overwrite it.
2. Set H2 to match how you keyed in your takings. For most hawkers, that is the inclusive setting.
3. Copy your July to September daily figures into v1.3.
4. Compare the new Box 6 figure on the quarterly tab with the output tax you filed. Box 1 should not change.
5. Write down the difference and keep both files together with your Q3 records.
6. Do not adjust your next return on your own just yet. IRAS has its own rules on whether an error like this can be corrected in a later GST F5 or needs a GST F7. Please read the IRAS page on correcting errors in GST returns, or ask whoever does your filing, before you do anything.
7. From now on, use v1.3 for your Q4 records.

**If you have not filed yet**

Switch to v1.3 now, set H2, and copy your figures across before you file.

**Thank you**

Ravi Subramaniam spotted that his $1,090 day did not look right and took the trouble to ask. Shu Fen of Numbers For Hawkers confirmed the formula problem and told me to put up a proper post instead of burying the correction in a comment. Both of you saved a lot of people from filing another quarter with the wrong figure. Thank you.

If something in your own figures does not make sense after you re-run them, leave a comment below. I will reply.

Joanne
